annotationRationale: The arithmetic-series formula, integer divisibility, and a bound from positivity determine all three parameters. The supplied approaches share this core argument, so one complete route is sufficient.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate despite the supporting number-theory steps; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The unique admissible parameters are \(a=5,d=2,n=13\), whose true sum is 221 and whose requested sum is 20. A single increase of 1 produces the written total 222. Choice B and the supplied prompt/key agree.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: One complete method is sufficient. The reference factor-pair and middle-term approaches share the same arithmetic-sum divisibility structure and do not add a necessary distinct route.
review.annotationCheck: Arithmetic-series sums and integer-equation reasoning are correctly assessed. Prime factorization appropriately supports the divisor restriction.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate despite the supporting number-theory steps; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The true sum is 221 or 223. Positivity and integer d>1 give \(S\ge n^2\), hence \(3\le n\le14\), while the sum formula gives \(n\mid2S\). The supplied prime check excludes 223; the factorization of 442 leaves only n=13. Then \(a+6d=17\), a≥1 and integer d≥2 force d=2 and a=5. Existence and the final value 20 are verified.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE reference supplies the complete positivity-bound and divisibility route. AoPS provides related factor approaches, some with incomplete exclusions; the candidate does not inherit those gaps. The explanation expands the reasoning in original prose and honestly uses source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The length bound makes the divisor search visibly finite. Integrality of d, primality of 223, uniqueness of d and consistency with the writing error are all explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h204 supplies the sum formula, math:integer-diophantine-equations captures the bounded integer search, and math:prime-factorization supports complete divisor exclusion.
